notes: #5 is a 1635 printing of the vol. 1 plate (1572), uncolored; the colored copies are unusable (#3 has a hole over the town, #4 and #6 have a book gutter through the view, #1 is only 1024 px). The plate’s Latin text box overlaps the sky at right and can’t be trimmed without losing that end of the town. #9: the record and file name give Topographia Hassiae, 1655; if this plate first appeared in Topographia Palatinatus Rheni (1645), its year should be 1645 and it would clash with #5 in P1. #13 and #11 are 42 years apart. #15 is the same photochrom as #11. #8 is a detail of a Merian plate; #7 is Pfeddersheim, #10 another Palatinate town.
